snippet.title: [PC-98] Star Striker - ALL Clear 1,969,576 (No-Miss)
snippet.description:
Epilepsy warning.

Turn on captions for some extra comments.

Star Striker is an absolutely out of control 1995 doujin PC-98 shmup from Promisence Soft. 
This pushes the PC-98 so much to its limits that it's basically the Recca of PC-98.

Okay so I thought the engine used in Atomic Punker never made it further than the proof of concept tech demo that was Atomic Punker, but apparently there was an actual game made with it!
Star Striker makes full use of this insane engine to do some absolutely bonkers effects and stage design.

Atomic Punker was basically a tech demo showcasing this insane PC-98 shmup engine. 
It was first submitted to a game jam by this 18-year old kid and the levels of smoothness, effects and sprites on screen was just absolutely mental for PC-98. It was better than anything commercially made for the PC-98 and was even rivaling arcade hardware at the time. 
I made a video on this game as well. 

You can definitely see shades of Atomic Punker in this game. 
A lot of enemy behavior and patterns are carried over into this game, and the thing about enemies spawning on the opposite side of the screen is also used in this, though not as prevalent.

Star Striker plays very different from Atomic Punker though. 
It's a lot more akin to enemy hell than bullet hell. The game throws a crazy amount of popcorn enemies at you at super high speeds that you have to shoot down before they ram you. A lot of enemy waves also remind me of something you'd see in Star Force。

- System
The system is a bit different from Atomic Punker. 
Your shot is now straight instead of wide and has homing missiles. The homing missiles are fairly powerful. 
Bombs and items got removed in favor of this dash mechanic that gives you i-frames. 
You have to hold down the button and there is like a one second cooldown on it so you can't spam it. It's also really easy to just dash straight into another bullet once it runs out. The big downside to the dash is that you cannot shoot while it's active, and that can easily get you killed in this game. 
Hitboxes aren't huge but they're not small either.
Atomic Punker started you off with 13 lives but this game just gives you straight-up infinite lives.
The only punishment for dying is that you lose score, which is quite a bizarre design decision. 

- Survival
Clearing is trivial because of the infinite lives but the patterns themselves are quite tricky to dodge. You have to be really aggressive with your enemy killing to not get completely overwhelmed. 
This game is also a lot more random, enemy waves have a lot more random elements to them. There is one section in stage 5 where you just have to pray enemies don't ram you, it's jacked. Your homing lasers also aren't the most reliable thing. 
All of the bosses are pushovers except for the final boss, this boss would be a lot harder if it wasn't for the safespot. I align my shot on a section of the boss to line myself up with the safespot. 
Trouble spots are stage 3, 5 and the final boss.

- Scoring
Scoring is survival. 
Dying makes you lose a percentage of your score every time you die.
There aren't any destructible bullets or missiles either so there's nothing else besides that and enemy destruction. 
A lot of enemies are quite hard to kill though, as they leave the screen really fast. 
Score loss from death being percentage based makes later deaths a lot more painful than early ones. 

I'm not sure if I like this game better than Atomic Punker, which is kind of ironic. 
The bosses feel like a downgrade, the shot is less satisfying and this has more dead air.
Getting randomly rammed by enemies that you can't do anything about is also pretty frustrating.  
Also stage 4 just sucks with all the flashing and the boss is just garbage.   
Stage 3 and 5 are great though, the fast-paced parts are a lot more fast-paced and this has a lot more enemy variety. This definitely has the better visual experience with the crazy background scrolling and the onslaught of enemies, though the sound effects are not nearly as satisfying.  
The engrish is also 10/10.
